eyebrow: The single highest-value SSH hardening step
code:
# /etc/ssh/sshd_config
PasswordAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin no

$ sudo systemctl reload sshd
caption: reload, not restart — keeps existing sessions alive while applying the change

eyebrow: Firewall on Ubuntu — allow SSH before you enable it
code:
$ sudo ufw allow 22/tcp
$ sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
$ sudo ufw enable
$ sudo ufw status
Status: active
22/tcp   ALLOW   Anywhere
caption: Enabling with no rule for your own connection locks you out immediately

code:
$ sudo firewall-cmd --add-service=ssh --permanent
$ sudo firewall-cmd --add-service=https --permanent
$ sudo firewall-cmd --reload
$ sudo firewall-cmd --list-services
ssh https
caption: --permanent persists across reboots; --reload applies it without dropping connections
